title: Autoscaler: blend reactive + forecast desired replicas with confidence gating and safety margins
author: Keiko Yamamoto
release_notes: - Dedicated autoscaler can optionally incorporate short-horizon demand forecasts when selecting desired replicas (bounded + cooldown-aware).
body: Summary Implements the predictive blending algorithm for Dedicated pool autoscaling by combining reactive signals (queue depth, utilization/latency derived desired) with forecast-based desired replicas (from Predictive Signal Service), gated by forecast confidence and guarded by safety margins and scale rate limits. This is the core logic behind ENG-2845 and builds on the ingestion/scaffolding added in PR #21941. Motivation Our current reactive controller is prone to (a) ramp-up latency spikes during sudden load increases and (b) oscillation when queue depth is bursty. The forecast signal helps pre-scale, but must be safe: if the forecast is wrong we must degrade gracefully to reactive behavior and never violate customer bounds or cooldown policies. Design overview (high level) The controller now computes three candidate desired values each tick: 1) reactive_desired computed by existing logic (queue depth + p95 latency + GPU saturation), 2) forecast_desired derived from forecasted token rate/QPS and observed per-GPU capacity, and 3) bounded_desired = clamp(blended_desired, min_replicas, max_replicas) from evaluated policy config. Blending algorithm (pseudo) Inputs: reactive_desired, forecast_desired, forecast_confidence (0..1), cfg.confidence_threshold, cfg.safety_margin_pct, cfg.max_forecast_overshoot_replicas, cfg.prefer_forecast_on_scale_up, cfg.cooldowns/scale-rate limits. Steps: - If forecast missing/stale (> cfg.max_forecast_age_seconds) -> blended = reactive_desired; gate_reason=forecast_stale. - Else if forecast_confidence < cfg.confidence_threshold -> blended = reactive_desired; gate_reason=low_confidence. - Else compute forecast_with_margin = ceil(forecast_desired * (1 + safety_margin_pct)). - For scale-up ticks: blended = max(reactive_desired, forecast_with_margin) when cfg.prefer_forecast_on_scale_up=true, otherwise blended = reactive_desired + ceil((forecast_with_margin - reactive_desired) * cfg.forecast_weight). - For scale-down ticks: blended = min(reactive_desired, forecast_with_margin) to avoid forecasting driving aggressive scale-down; scale-down remains primarily reactive. - Cap forecast influence: blended is additionally capped so it cannot exceed reactive_desired + cfg.max_forecast_overshoot_replicas (prevents runaway pre-scale on outlier forecasts). - Apply cooldown + scale-rate limits after blending, before min/max clamp, to keep decision reasoning consistent and avoid clamp/cooldown deadlocks. Cooldown interactions - Previously the code effectively treated “desired after clamp” as the value to feed into cooldown bookkeeping, which could cause undesirable behavior where a bounded desired would continuously “re-arm” the cooldown window without any actuation change. This PR changes cooldown bookkeeping to track (a) the last_applied_replicas and (b) the last_directional_change (up/down), and then apply cooldown decisions against the proposed actuation delta, not the pre-clamp target. - Scale-up cooldown does not block emergency scale-up paths triggered by the existing “SLO protection” branch (p95 latency > threshold AND queue rising); in those cases we still prefer reactive_desired but allow bypassing forecast gating (gate_reason=slo_protect). Observability / explainability - Adds structured decision fields to the autoscaler decision log to support Console audit trail: reactive_desired, forecast_desired, forecast_confidence, forecast_age_ms, blend_mode (reactive_only|max_reactive_forecast|weighted|slo_protect), gate_reason (ok|forecast_stale|low_confidence|missing|slo_protect), applied_cooldown (none|scale_up|scale_down), and overshoot_cap_applied (true/false). - Metrics emitted follow existing cardinality guardrails: values are numeric gauges/counters tagged by pool_id hash + region + hardware_class (no raw customer identifiers). Testing - Unit tests cover gating (missing/stale/low confidence), max-reactive-forecast path, overshoot cap, and scale-down behavior (forecast cannot trigger faster scale-down than reactive). - Simulation tests run 30-minute synthetic traces to validate: (1) no oscillation regression compared to baseline and (2) bounded max with forecast enabled does not exceed max_replicas even with high confidence forecasts. - Added regression test for cooldown bookkeeping to ensure we do not get stuck when clamp + cooldown both apply. Rollout notes This change is behind the existing bounded-autoscaling feature flag (see #21927). Predictive blending is further gated by evaluated config (predictive_enabled + confidence_threshold). We can enable per allowlisted pool. Linked work - ENG-2845 - Depends on #21941 for forecast ingestion scaffolding - Pairs with metrics work in #21912/#21912 follow-ups (this PR only adds decision fields/logging; dashboarding handled elsewhere).
commits: autoscaler: implement blendReactiveAndForecastDesired() helper with gating
autoscaler: restructure cooldown bookkeeping to be delta-based
autoscaler: add overshoot cap + safety margin handling
tests: add blend/gating unit tests + cooldown regression tests
logging: include blend_mode and gate_reason in decision logs
review_conversation: Vanessa Ortiz: I like the general approach, but I’m concerned about forecast driving scale-down. Can we make sure forecast never increases the rate of scale-down vs reactive? Keiko Yamamoto: Good call. Updated logic so scale-down uses min(reactive, forecast_with_margin) and also keeps scale-down primarily reactive. Added unit test `TestBlend_ScaleDownForecastDoesNotAccelerate`. Karthik Iyer: Two requests: (1) guard against stale forecasts (clock skew / pipeline stalls) and (2) cap how far forecast can overshoot reactive to avoid pre-scaling to max on a single spiky prediction. Keiko Yamamoto: Added max_forecast_age_seconds gating (default 90s) with gate_reason=forecast_stale and added `max_forecast_overshoot_replicas` (default 8) cap. Included both in decision logs for auditability. Jordan Lee: Please confirm ordering with policy bounds + cooldown. We’ve had clamp/cooldown interactions cause surprising behavior (see previous incident threads). The logic should be easy to explain: decide -> cooldown/rate-limit -> clamp -> apply. Keiko Yamamoto: Agreed. Refactored to apply cooldown/rate-limit before min/max clamp and changed cooldown bookkeeping to track last_applied_replicas rather than last_desired. Added regression test covering clamp + cooldown scenario. Allison Grant: From an observability standpoint, we need a stable set of reason codes for Console. Avoid free-form strings. Also ensure we don’t introduce high-cardinality tags in metrics. Keiko Yamamoto: Updated to enum-like reason codes (ok, missing, forecast_stale, low_confidence, slo_protect) and ensured metrics tags remain region/hardware_class/pool_hash only. Added `blend_mode` and `gate_reason` as low-cardinality string fields in logs (not tags). Logan Wright: CI failed on the sim test due to nondeterministic random seed in `synthetic_traces_test`. Can we make it deterministic? Keiko Yamamoto: Fixed by seeding with a constant and moved the random generator into the test harness; reran CI. Vanessa Ortiz: Approving after the scale-down change and cooldown ordering refactor. Karthik Iyer: Approving. Please make sure defaults are conservative. Jordan Lee: Approving. Allison Grant: Approving (thanks for keeping reason codes tight).
